overview_markdown:
LobsterAI is an open-source desktop agent from NetEase Youdao, billed as the first desktop-grade agent open-sourced by a major Chinese tech company. Architecturally, it splits responsibilities: the Cowork layer (Electron 40 + React 18 desktop app) owns local persistence, permissions, UI state, artifacts, agents, memory, and IM bindings, while OpenClaw serves as the underlying agent runtime and gateway.

Its standout features include long-running cowork sessions against local files and projects with approval gates for sensitive actions (file ops, terminal commands, network access), multi-agent workflows with per-agent identity/model/skills, and Expert Kits that package scenario-specific capabilities. A key differentiator is phone-based remote control through WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, and Telegram — clearly aimed at the Chinese office productivity market.

Compared to running OpenClaw directly, LobsterAI trades leanness for usability: you get a polished GUI, structured releases (currently at 2026.9.4 with active CI maintenance), and desktop-native workflows, but at the cost of an Electron memory footprint, macOS/Windows-only support, and some vendor server-side configuration endpoints that temper its otherwise local-first posture.
